info.title: CF Meet Calling service API
info.description: HTTP surface exposed by services/calling (Part C sections 15-25): the health endpoint; the call API (list, get, available actions); application call creation (POST /v1/calls) and control (accept, decline, cancel, end, hold, resume, transfer, session removal, media credentials); the application endpoint registry and signaling-credential minting; the endpoint's own signaling operations (WebSocket channel, offer recovery, accept / decline, media credentials) authenticated by a short-lived signaling credential; the media connection gateway, which admits every media signaling connection against authoritative state before the media server is contacted; and the media provider callback, authenticated by the provider's signature. There is no generic state mutation: a client never sends a state, a scope, an authorization result, a route, a provider, a room, a media identity, a permission or a telephone number. Tenant, application and environment scope comes only from the authenticated credential; a call, principal, endpoint, offer or session of another scope is answered exactly like a missing one (404). Every state-changing command carries expectedVersion (the single concurrency mechanism); Idempotency-Key is required for call creation and transfer and honoured on every other command (a replay returns the recorded response with Idempotent-Replayed: true; a different request under the same key is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT). Every response carries an x-request-id header with the server-generated request id; a well-formed client x-request-id is echoed as x-client-request-id. 1.12.0 the Part VI §53 webhook migration export (GET /internal/v1/webhook-migration/{inventory,digest,subscriptions,events,deliveries,attempts}, webhook-migration.export; signing secrets only re-sealed under the migration transfer key) and rollback (POST /internal/v1/webhook-migration/rollback/{subscriptions,deliveries}, webhook-migration.import); customer webhook routes answer 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with CF-Webhook-Migration: frozen (mutations, CALLING_WEBHOOK_MUTATIONS_FROZEN) or moved (CALLING_WEBHOOK_AUTHORITY=retired).

post.description: Receives a restrictive enforcement command from Privacy Relay (contract cfmeet.privacy-relay.enforcement-command). Requires an internal service token, the receiver-granted permission communication-authority.enforce (grantable only to cfmeet.privacy-relay) and a signed delegated platform context (the only scope). Calling finds its own protected calls by the opaque communication_context_ref / privacy_relay_ref it stored, skips calls authorized at or after the enforced version, and terminates the rest through the ordinary call commands (pre-answer CANCEL; answered / connected / held / transferring END -> ENDING -> cleanup -> ENDED). Deduplicated by enforcementEventId: a replay returns the recorded result without touching calls again. It can never grant authority.

200.description: Applied (or the recorded result of the same enforcement event).

post.description: Receives one normalized event from Telephony's outbox (contract cfmeet.telephony.event): requires an internal service token with the receiver-granted permission telephony-event.apply (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Calling deduplicates by eventId, applies per-leg sequences in order (an older one is STALE), quarantines events that do not match an execution it commanded (UNMATCHED) and never resurrects a terminal Call (IGNORED_TERMINAL; a late success triggers cleanup of the execution). Every delivered event is answered 200 with its disposition; only a failure to record it is an error (Telephony retries). Telephony never sets Calling state: each event is validated against Calling's own state machines. No telephone number, provider id or SIP data exists in the body.

200.description: Recorded with its disposition (APPLIED, DUPLICATE, STALE, IGNORED_TERMINAL or UNMATCHED).

post.description: Telephony offers an inbound public call to a relay number (contract cfmeet.telephony.inbound-offer). Requires an internal service token with telephony-inbound.offer (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Calling re-checks CURRENT Privacy Relay authority (CALLBACK_RELAY route), the routing policy (PSTN_TO_APP), the environment's configured inbound owner and the spend policy, then creates ONE canonical Call (origin PUBLIC_INBOUND; the caller is a TELEPHONE_ENDPOINT principal referencing only the opaque ContactReference) and rings the authorized application principals. Idempotent per telephonyLegId. Refusals reveal nothing to the caller.

200.description: The canonical Call and public CallLeg (the same for a repeated offer).

get.summary: List the caller's calls, or one principal's call history (newest first, keyset pagination)
get.description: Requires the calls.read scope. Ordered by createdAt descending, then callId descending. Only the bounded filters below are accepted; unknown or repeated query parameters are rejected with 400. The cursor is opaque, carries position only and never scope. Part F §62: with principalId the response is that principal's canonical call history (CallHistoryList): only Calls it participates in, each with its participant-relative direction and outcome derived from Call evidence (never from push or realtime delivery), safe enterprise labels, the voicemail link for mailbox owners and recording availability; direction / outcome / missed need principalId. enterpriseDestinationType + enterpriseDestinationId narrow either listing.

post.summary: Create and ring an application call
post.description: Requires calls.write and an Idempotency-Key. Creates the Call (REQUESTED), records the APP_DIRECT_V1 authorization, resolves the target principals inside the credential's scope, selects the APPLICATION route, prepares the Call's media resource through the configured media provider, authorizes the initiator's session and rings every eligible endpoint of every target (one offer each, server-owned expiry). Answers 201 with the call (normally RINGING). A replay with the same key returns the recorded response; the call is never created twice.

201.description: The call was created (or the recorded response of an identical earlier request).

post.summary: Accept a ring offer on behalf of one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Exactly one device per participant wins (single-winner arbitration in the database); the participant's other offers become ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE and lose every media path. The first winning participant moves the Call to ANSWERED. An expired offer is 410; an offer that is no longer live (cancelled, answered elsewhere, declined) is 409.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Decline a ring offer on behalf of one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Declines only this endpoint's offer; other devices keep ringing. The Call ends as DECLINED only when every live offer of every pending target is declined.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Cancel a call before it is active
post.description: Requires calls.write. Pre-active termination (REQUESTED ... ANSWERED): cancels live offers and outstanding attempts, closes route, leg and sessions and tears down the media resource. Repeating it on a CANCELLED call is a no-op.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.description: Requires calls.write. Moves the Call to ENDING, removes every media connection and terminates the media resource; the Call becomes ENDED only on cleanup evidence (otherwise it stays ENDING and the reconciler retries). Usage and quality are finalized.

post.description: Requires calls.write. Enforced at the media provider: every admitted connection loses audio and video publishing (subscription unchanged) before the Call becomes HELD. 200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.description: Requires calls.write. Re-derives every connection's permissions from the currently authorized server state (never from a stored pre-hold grant) and applies them at the provider before the Call becomes CONNECTED.

post.summary: Transfer a participant's place to another principal
post.description: Requires calls.write and an Idempotency-Key. The same Call continues (TRANSFERRING): the target's endpoints are rung with TRANSFER offers; when the target joins with a media path the transferring participant is retired and the Call returns to CONNECTED. If the target declines, does not answer or cannot join, the transfer FAILS and the Call returns to its pre-transfer state (CONNECTED or HELD) when the remaining parties still have a media path.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Issue a media credential for a session
post.description: Requires calls.write. Issues a short-lived join credential for one session whose media access the server authorized (the initiator's session, or a participant's single winning device) while the Call is in a media state. Capabilities derive from server state only; the body must be empty. A losing, removed or ended session, or a terminal Call, is 409.

post.summary: Remove one session from a call
post.description: Requires calls.write. Ends the session and revokes its media access for ever: its credentials stop working, the provider connection is removed (or queued for enforcement) and any re-entry is evicted. The Call's state is not changed; removing a removed session again is a no-op.

200.description: The session was removed (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Register an application endpoint of a principal
post.description: Requires calls.write. The principal is resolved inside the credential's scope (unknown, foreign or inactive: 404). Registering the same endpointKey again for the same principal refreshes the endpoint (200); a key held by another principal is 409.

get.description: Requires calls.read. Only endpoints of the credential's scope; a foreign principal has none.

delete.description: Requires calls.write. The endpoint is never rung again; its live offers are cancelled and its signaling credentials stop working. Revoking a revoked endpoint is a no-op.

post.summary: Mint a signaling credential for one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Called by the application backend, which hands the short-lived credential to the device. The device never receives the platform API credential.

get.summary: Open the endpoint's realtime signaling channel (WebSocket)
get.description: Authenticated before the upgrade with the endpoint's signaling credential. Delivery only: the server sends signaling.ready, then the endpoint's realtime signals (cfmeet.calling.realtime-signal, https://schemas.cfmeet.com/calling/realtime/v1.schema.json), answers {"type":"ping"} with signaling.pong and closes with code 4001 when the credential expires. Signals are sent only after the authoritative transaction committed; a lost signal never loses state (recover with GET /v1/calling/invitations and the call API). Commands use HTTP.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the WebSocket channel is open (subprotocol cfmeet.signaling.v1 when it was offered).

get.description: Signaling credential. The endpoint's live and recently finished offers with the authoritative Call state; only unexpired RINGING offers of answerable calls are actionable. Stale client state is never trusted.

get.summary: Open a media signaling connection (SDK legacy path)
get.description: Media connection gateway (WebSocket upgrade; the media SDK's signaling protocol is relayed opaquely). Before anything reaches the media server, the presented media credential is authenticated (edge signature, expiry, resource, identity, generation) and admitted against authoritative state: the session must exist in that Call, hold media access (AUTHORIZED, not removed or ended, participant still in the Call, Call in a media state) and the credential must carry the session's CURRENT media generation. Otherwise the upgrade is refused (401; 503 when the state cannot be read: fail closed). An admitted connection is relayed with a single-use, join-only media-server token; media rights are applied server-side after the join. Every token the media server refreshes is re-checked and re-sealed with the edge key before it reaches the client, so no client ever holds a token the media server accepts directly.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the admitted connection is relayed to the media server.

400.description: Malformed request (query, or no WebSocket upgrade).

401.description: Not admitted: missing, malformed, forged or expired credential; unknown identity; foreign resource; revoked, removed or ended session; stale generation; terminal Call. Plain-text body; uniform.

503.description: Authoritative state unreadable, or the media server unreachable: refused (fail closed).

post.description: Part F: Telephony offers an internal enterprise SIP dialog (contract cfmeet.telephony.enterprise). Requires an internal service token with telephony-enterprise.offer (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Calling binds the opaque device reference to its ACTIVE principal in the offer's scope, resolves the extension there, applies the enterprise policy and the environment's configured owner, then creates ONE canonical Call (origin ENTERPRISE_DEVICE, route class ENTERPRISE_INTERNAL; the dialog is a PRIVATE_NETWORK leg) and routes it (ring, ring group, queue, IVR). Idempotent per telephonyLegId. An unknown / foreign device or extension is 404; enterprise calling off is 422.

200.description: The canonical Call and public CallLeg (the same for a repeated offer).

post.description: Part F: one key of an enterprise SIP leg's caller for the IVR the Call waits in (contract cfmeet.telephony.enterprise). Requires telephony-enterprise.offer. The key is used once and never stored or logged; accepted=false when the Call does not wait for a key.

200.description: The canonical Call and public CallLeg (the same for a repeated offer).

post.description: Part F: Telephony delivers a finished or failed edge media capture (contract cfmeet.telephony.capture). Requires telephony-capture.deliver (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Only a SIP capture Calling asked for, on that leg, is accepted (anything else is 404). The audio is integrity-checked (size, SHA-256, audio/wav, bounded length) and stored in protected object storage; the message becomes READY. 200 = stored or acknowledged (the edge may delete its spool copy); 503 ARTIFACT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE = retry later; 400 = refused for good.

Requires enterprise.config.write. Typed rules only. isDefault makes it the environment's baseline (the previous default is cleared, a versioned change). Enabling public forwarding or granting MANAGE_PUBLIC_FORWARDING / MANAGE_RECORDING needs that capability in the current baseline (granted by a CF Meet operator): otherwise 403 ENTERPRISE_POLICY_DENIED. Audited.

CommandConflict.description: The command cannot apply to the current state: STALE_CALL_VERSION (expectedVersion is not the current version), CALL_STATE_CONFLICT, CALL_RESOURCE_STATE_CONFLICT, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (same key, different request), CONFLICT (the command with this key is still in progress), INVITATION_NOT_ACTIONABLE, ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE (another device of the participant won) or TARGET_UNAVAILABLE.

InvitationExpired.description: The offer expired (server-owned expiry); it can never be accepted. Code INVITATION_EXPIRED.

Unprocessable.description: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (the configured media provider cannot execute or enforce the operation), PARTICIPANT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED or CALL_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

TooManyRequests.description: RATE_LIMITED (request-rate limit) or CONCURRENT_CALL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (the environment's concurrent-call limit).

Unavailable.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (database) or MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE (the media provider did not confirm the operation; the state is unchanged or queued for enforcement and reconciliation).

SignalingAuthenticationFailed.description: Missing, malformed, expired or no longer valid signaling credential (revoked endpoint, inactive principal, revoked minting credential), or a platform API credential. Uniform for every reason. Code AUTHENTICATION_FAILED.

EnterpriseForbidden.description: INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE (the credential lacks the operation's enterprise scope; calls.* never implies it) or ENTERPRISE_POLICY_DENIED (the organization's enterprise policy does not grant this capability or action).

EnterpriseConflict.description: VERSION_CONFLICT (expectedVersion is not the current version; nothing changed) or CONFLICT (an active name / extension number already exists, the resource is disabled, or it is still referenced).

Call.description: One call with participants, session summaries and durations. Durations of open connections are measured up to durationsAsOf (the call's end for terminal calls). connectedDurationMs runs from the first CONNECTED to the end (null if never connected). invitations are the Call's ring offers (one per target endpoint and ring round); transfers its application transfers.

CallCounterpart.description: Another participant of the Call (internal display identity only).

CallHistoryEnterprise.description: Safe enterprise labels of an enterprise Call: the dialed internal extension (a short code or alias, never a telephone number), its label, the routing phase / outcome and the current ring group / queue labels.

CallHistoryEntry.description: A Call as it appears in one principal's history.

durationMs.description: From CONNECTED to the end of the Call; null while it lasts or if it never connected.

recordingAvailable.description: A READY call recording exists (metadata and audio through the authorized, audited recording routes).

CallHistoryList.description: One page of a principal's call history, newest Call first (createdAt DESC, callId DESC).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor of the next page; null on the last page.

CallHistoryVoicemail.description: The voicemail message left on the Call — present only for an owner of its mailbox. Its audio is reached through the authorized, audited voicemail routes (never a URL here).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor of the next page; null on the last page.

CallParticipant.description: A logical participant. displayName is presentation metadata only and never identifies anyone. connectedDurationMs is the union of the participant's session connection intervals (concurrent devices are not double counted).

CallParticipation.description: The principal's own part in the Call (one per logical participant, whatever its devices).

answeredAt.description: When the participant (any device) answered; for the initiator, when the Call was answered.

CallSession.description: Summary of one device / network participation of a participant (its media / signaling identity is not exposed). connectionCount is the number of connection intervals opened (1 + reconnects). endpointId is the application endpoint the session runs on; mediaAccess is NONE until the server authorizes the session's media (initiator, or the participant's single winning device), REVOKED for ever after removal; mediaAdmittedAt is when the provider confirmed an admitted connection; removedAt is set when the session was removed.

ErrorCode.description: Stable public error codes of the Calling service.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Error response body. Messages are fixed, safe strings; authentication failures are uniform.

HistoryDestinationType.description: Enterprise destinations a listing may be narrowed to.

HistoryDirection.description: Direction of a Call relative to the principal whose history it is.

ParticipantOutcome.description: The outcome of a Call for ONE logical participant, derived from Call evidence only (participant, ring offers on every device, session connection intervals, the Call's state) — never from a push, a realtime signal or a client acknowledgement, and never stored as a flag. OUTBOUND: ANSWERED, NOT_ANSWERED (ended unanswered), IN_PROGRESS. INBOUND, first match wins: ANSWERED (an offer accepted on any of the participant's devices, or a session connected), DECLINED, ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE (the offers were won by another participant of the same answer group — a ring-group or queue colleague), RINGING (an offer is live), MISSED (offered on at least one device and every offer ended unanswered), NOT_REACHED (never offered, Call over), IN_PROGRESS. A losing device of a participant that answered is never a second (missed) entry.

calling.common.v1.CallCore.description: Fields of every Call representation (HTTP API, call-control results). Provider-independent: no provider or carrier identifiers, execution bindings, media identities, telephone numbers or protected contact data.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version: 1 at creation, +1 per state transition.

endedAt.description: When the call reached a terminal state.

calling.common.v1.CallEndpointKind.description: Neutral kind of a registered application endpoint (a device / client instance of a principal).

calling.common.v1.CallEndpointPresence.description: Presence hint used to order ringing; never an authorization.

calling.common.v1.CallFailureCategory.description: Normalized failure category. Provider error codes never become categories.

calling.common.v1.CallInvitationPurpose.description: Why a ring offer exists: the Call itself, or an application transfer to a new target.

calling.common.v1.CallInvitationStatus.description: State of a ring offer to one endpoint. PENDING and RINGING are live; every other state is terminal and final (an offer is never revived). The server owns expiry.

calling.common.v1.CallKind.description: Neutral media kind of a Call. No consumer business meaning.

calling.common.v1.CallMediaAccess.description: A session's media authority: NONE until the server authorizes it (initiator, or the single winning device of a participant), AUTHORIZED while it may hold media credentials, REVOKED for ever after removal or the end of the session.

calling.common.v1.CallMediaCapabilities.description: Media capabilities the server authorizes for one session's media connection. Derived from server state (call kind, participant permissions, hold); never chosen by the client. There is no administrative, recording, room-creation or room-listing capability.

calling.common.v1.CallState.description: Canonical business state of a Call. Terminal: ENDED, DECLINED, BUSY, NO_ANSWER, FAILED, CANCELLED.

calling.common.v1.CallSummary.description: A call as listed and as returned by call-control commands.

calling.common.v1.CallTerminalReason.description: How a Call reached its terminal state. ENDED records its completion evidence; every other terminal state has the reason of the same name.

calling.common.v1.CallTransferFailureRea.description: Why a transfer did not complete. A failed transfer returns the Call to its pre-transfer state when the remaining parties still have a media path.

calling.common.v1.CallTransferState.description: Application transfer lifecycle, kept out of the Call state (the Call is TRANSFERRING while a transfer is active).

calling.common.v1.SafeEventData.description: Bounded, flat, privacy-safe event data: at most 32 snake_case keys that never name secrets, credentials, contact data or provider / carrier identifiers; values are booleans, numbers, safe text or short lists of safe text.

calling.common.v1.SafeText.description: Bounded text without control characters that never looks like a telephone number (+<digit>) or a tel: / sip: URI.

calling.control.v1.AcceptResult.description: The offer was accepted: this endpoint's device won its participant's answer (single winner), the participant's other offers became ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE, and sessionId is the winning session that may now request media credentials. callAnswered is true when this acceptance moved the Call to ANSWERED.

reason.description: Why the action is unavailable: the credential lacks calls.write, the Call's state does not allow it, or the configured media provider cannot enforce it.

calling.control.v1.AvailableActions.description: Server-derived actions currently valid for a Call and the authenticated credential. The client never computes them from local state.

calling.control.v1.CallInvitation.description: A ring offer of a Call to one endpoint of one target participant. Status and terminal reason always agree: an offer that expired, was cancelled or was answered elsewhere can never be accepted, and a live offer has neither.

calling.control.v1.CallTransfer.description: An application transfer of a Call (kept out of the Call state).

calling.control.v1.CommandRequest.description: Body of cancel, end, hold, resume and session removal: the expected Call version and nothing else (no state, reason or permission can be sent).

expectedVersion.description: The Call version the command was decided on (optimistic concurrency). A different current version is refused with 409 STALE_CALL_VERSION.

calling.control.v1.ControlResult.description: Result of cancel, end, hold and resume: the Call after the command. END answers with ENDING until provider cleanup is confirmed, or ENDED once it is.

calling.control.v1.CreateCallRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/calls. The initiator calls from one of its registered ACTIVE endpoints; every target is a principal of the same application environment (resolved inside the credential's scope; an unknown or foreign principal is 404). One target is a one-to-one call, several targets a group call (at most the configured participant limit, 16 by default, including the initiator). The server decides authorization, routing, ringing and media; nothing of that can be sent. Part E: instead of principal targets, ONE protected public-network contact (targetContactReference, an opaque ContactReference issued by Privacy Relay — never a telephone number) under a Privacy Relay Session: an APP_TO_PSTN call executed by Telephony after Privacy Relay (PUBLIC_RELAY), the Routing Engine, the telecom switches and a durable spend reservation all allow it (403 PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED / 503 PUBLIC_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE / 429 TELECOM_SPEND_LIMIT_EXCEEDED otherwise). The caller identity is selected server-side; no request field can set it. Part E §47 callback relay: callbackRequested with the requester's own verified protected contact (initiatorContactReference) and the callee's (targetContactReference) under a Privacy Relay Session, without an endpoint: Telephony calls the requester first and the callee only after the first leg answered; both legs are bridged in one Call (two legs, two usage facts).

initiatorEndpointId.description: The initiator's registered ACTIVE endpoint. Required for application and APP_TO_PSTN calls; absent for a callback relay.

callbackRequested.description: The requester asks to be called back on its own protected contact and bridged to the callee (Part E §47). A request, not a route: Privacy Relay and the Routing Engine decide whether CALLBACK_RELAY is allowed (403 PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED otherwise).

initiatorContactReference.description: The requester's own verified protected contact (callback relay only).

targetContactReference.description: A protected contact (opaque ContactReference). Requires privacyRelaySessionId; exclusive with targetPrincipalIds.

privacyRelaySessionId.description: Optional Privacy Relay Session (cfmeet.privacy-relay.session). The call becomes a PROTECTED call: Calling asks Privacy Relay for current authority (PRIVACY_RELAY_V1) before anything rings, records the decision and fails closed (503 PRIVACY_AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE) when no answer can be obtained; it never falls back to APP_DIRECT_V1. VOICE only. A transfer of a protected call re-authorizes the new target.

targetExtension.description: Part F: an enterprise extension number (an internal short code, never a telephone number) resolved in the credential's scope and routed by enterprise configuration over ENTERPRISE_INTERNAL (no public leg, no spend). Requires enterprise.calls.use and initiatorEndpointId; excludes every other target. An unknown number is 404; a policy refusal 403 CALL_NOT_AUTHORIZED; enterprise calling disabled 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE.

presentedNumberResourceId.description: Part IV L: a Digital Communications Number (CF Meet Number Resource id — never a telephone number) to present as the caller identity of a targetContactReference call instead of the session's relay identity. Numbering must hold it ACTIVE for the credential's scope with usable outbound voice, and the initiator must be entitled to present it: the owner of a personal / professional number, or an ACTIVE enterprise principal reached through an organization number's voice target (organizational scope alone never suffices). 403 PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED otherwise; 503 PUBLIC_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE while Numbering is unreachable. No other identity is ever substituted.

calling.control.v1.CreateCallResult.description: Response of POST /v1/calls (201; replays return the same body with Idempotent-Replayed: true). The call is normally RINGING with one live offer per eligible target endpoint; it can still be ROUTING while the media resource is being prepared (the reconciler resumes it), or already FAILED (ROUTING when no target has an eligible endpoint, MEDIA when the resource could not be prepared in time). Part F: an enterprise Call (targetExtension) additionally carries its enterprise context; while it waits in a queue or IVR it may list only the initiator.

enterprise.description: Present for an enterprise Call only: its safe enterprise context.

calling.control.v1.DeclineResult.description: The offer was declined. Only this endpoint's offer ends; the Call ends as DECLINED only when every live offer of every pending target has been declined.

calling.control.v1.EmptyRequest.description: A command without parameters (media credentials): an empty object or no body. The server derives every capability; any field is refused.

calling.control.v1.Endpoint.description: A registered application endpoint of a principal. Presence is a routing hint only.

endpointKey.description: Opaque client-chosen device key, unique per principal while ACTIVE. Never a telephone number or a tel: / sip: URI.

calling.control.v1.EndpointCapabilities.description: Media the endpoint can handle. Every application call needs audio: endpoints without audio are never rung; an audio-only endpoint is rung for VIDEO calls too and simply publishes no camera.

calling.control.v1.InvitationCommandRequ.description: Body of POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/accept|decline (backend answering on behalf of one of the target's endpoints).

expectedVersion.description: The Call version the command was decided on (optimistic concurrency). A different current version is refused with 409 STALE_CALL_VERSION.

calling.control.v1.MediaCredential.description: A short-lived join credential for one authorized session's connection to the Call's media resource: the connection URL, the opaque token, its expiry and the capabilities the connection receives once admitted. Room names, provider identifiers, provider keys and administrative grants are never part of it. A losing device, a removed session, an expired offer or a terminal Call never receives one.

url.description: Calling's media connection gateway URL (wss:// in production), never the media server itself.

token.description: Opaque join credential bound to this session's media identity, its current media generation and the Call's media resource, sealed by Calling's media edge: the media server does not accept it directly, and the gateway admits it only while that generation of the session holds media access. It carries no administrative grant.

calling.control.v1.ProviderCallbackAck.description: A verified media-provider callback was recorded (also for duplicates, which are no-ops).

calling.control.v1.RecoveredInvitation.description: An offer of the endpoint as recovered after a reconnect, with the authoritative Call state. actionable is true only for a RINGING, unexpired offer of a Call that can still be answered.

calling.control.v1.RecoveredInvitationLi.description: Response of GET /v1/calling/invitations (signaling credential): the endpoint's live and recently finished offers.

calling.control.v1.RegisterEndpointReque.description: Body of POST /v1/calling/endpoints. Registering the same key for the same principal again refreshes it (200).

endpointKey.description: Opaque client-chosen device key, unique per principal while ACTIVE. Never a telephone number or a tel: / sip: URI.

oneOf.description: Opaque reference to a push target held by the application (no push token).

calling.control.v1.SessionRemovalResult.description: Result of removing one session: its media access is revoked and the provider connection removed (or queued for enforcement).

calling.control.v1.SignalingCredential.description: A short-lived Call Signaling Credential for one endpoint, handed to the device by the application backend. It authenticates only the endpoint's own signaling operations and never a platform API operation; the platform API credential never reaches the device.

calling.control.v1.SignalingCredentialRe.description: Body of POST /v1/calling/signaling-credentials: one ACTIVE endpoint of one principal.

calling.control.v1.TransferRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/transfer (Idempotency-Key required): the participant who hands its place over, and the principal who takes it. The same Call continues; no second Call is created. Part F: exactly one target — a principal, an enterprise extension or a typed enterprise destination; an enterprise Call's policy must permit transfers (else 403).

expectedVersion.description: The Call version the command was decided on (optimistic concurrency). A different current version is refused with 409 STALE_CALL_VERSION.

targetExtension.description: Part F: an enterprise extension number resolved in the credential's scope (requires enterprise.calls.use). It is followed to ONE principal: a member directly, a ring group's first eligible member, a queue's first available agent, a schedule's current route.

targetDestination.description: Part F: a typed enterprise destination (ENTERPRISE_MEMBER, PRINCIPAL, EXTENSION, RING_GROUP, QUEUE or SCHEDULE of the same scope; requires enterprise.calls.use), resolved like targetExtension. A PUBLIC_CONTACT is refused: 403 when the enterprise policy forbids public forwarding, 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE otherwise (public transfer of an established call is not offered by this deployment).

calling.control.v1.TransferResult.description: Result of POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/transfer: the same Call (TRANSFERRING) and the transfer now ringing its target.

calling.enterprise.v1.ActivateIvrVersion.description: Body of PUT /v1/enterprise/ivr-flows/{ivr_flow_id}/activation: the published version NEW Calls run (Calls already in the IVR keep theirs). Its destinations are re-validated.

expectedVersion.description: The version the change was decided on. A different current version is refused with 409 VERSION_CONFLICT and changes nothing.

calling.enterprise.v1.AdminCapability.description: Organization-level administrative capabilities (second key after the credential's enterprise scopes). MANAGE_PUBLIC_FORWARDING and MANAGE_RECORDING are granted by a CF Meet operator only.

calling.enterprise.v1.AgentStatus.description: ACTIVE agents receive offers; PAUSED agents stay members but receive none.

calling.enterprise.v1.AuditRecord.description: Durable evidence of one administrative change (append-only). details holds bounded safe values only.

actorKind.description: Who the change is attributed to.

calling.enterprise.v1.BindSipDeviceReque.description: Body of POST /v1/enterprise/sip-devices: binds an operator-minted opaque device reference to an ACTIVE principal of the scope. Never a SIP URI, address, credential or number.

displayLabel.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

calling.enterprise.v1.BuiltinPrompt.description: The controlled built-in prompt catalog. The media plane plays its own copy (Telephony maps it to edge-local audio; an application client to its own asset). Never a URL, path, file name or synthesized text. Each prompt has a nominal length the media plane's audio must fit (WELCOME, MENU, NO_INPUT, GOODBYE 2 s; PLEASE_HOLD, TRANSFERRING, CLOSED 3 s; INVALID_OPTION 4 s; VOICEMAIL_GREETING 6 s; BEEP 1 s): a menu's input timer starts after the prompts it queued, and a HANGUP node's prompt plays for its nominal length before the platform ends the Call.

name.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

timezone.description: An IANA time-zone identifier (e.g. Africa/Lagos, Europe/London). Never a raw UTC offset: DST and historical offset changes come from the IANA database.

calling.enterprise.v1.CallPolicyList.description: A page of policies (keyset, creation order).

calling.enterprise.v1.CallRecording.description: A recording of ONE canonical Call. Integrity metadata only: never an object-storage key, a bucket, a stored URL, a telephone number or a provider identity (media through media-access).

calling.enterprise.v1.ConsentParticipant.description: Who must consent: NONE, every participant, or every participant other than the one requesting the recording (a system / administrator request: everyone).

openDestination.description: The OPEN route: an ENTERPRISE_MEMBER, PRINCIPAL, EXTENSION, RING_GROUP, QUEUE or IVR of the same scope.

closedDestination.description: The CLOSED route: an ENTERPRISE_MEMBER, PRINCIPAL, EXTENSION, RING_GROUP, QUEUE, IVR, VOICEMAIL or (where the enterprise policy permits public forwarding) a PUBLIC_CONTACT of the same scope.

name.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

calling.enterprise.v1.CreateExtensionReq.description: Body of POST /v1/enterprise/extensions. The number must match the governing policy's format, be unused and unambiguous (numeric extensions are never prefixes of each other) in the namespace (the credential's scope).

displayLabel.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

calling.enterprise.v1.CreateForwardingRu.description: Body of POST /v1/enterprise/forwarding-rules. At most one ACTIVE rule per principal and condition; an ALWAYS rule that would close a cycle of principals is refused (routing also stops loops with its visited set and hop budget).

destination.description: An ENTERPRISE_MEMBER, PRINCIPAL (not the owner), EXTENSION, RING_GROUP, QUEUE, IVR, VOICEMAIL or PUBLIC_CONTACT of the same scope. Never a number.

calling.enterprise.v1.CreatePublicContac.description: Body of POST /v1/enterprise/public-contacts: registers a PROTECTED public destination for forwarding / closed routes — an opaque Privacy Relay ContactReference and the Privacy Relay Session whose authority covers it. Never a telephone number. Requires an enterprise policy that permits public forwarding.

label.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

calling.enterprise.v1.CreateQueueRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/enterprise/queues. offerTimeoutSeconds is the ring time of one offer to one agent and is at most maxWaitSeconds.

name.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

overflow.description: Where a Call goes when the queue is full or its maximum wait elapses: an EXTENSION, RING_GROUP, another QUEUE, IVR or VOICEMAIL of the same scope (never the queue itself). Without one a full queue ends the Call BUSY and an elapsed wait NO_ANSWER.

calling.enterprise.v1.CreateRecordingPol.description: Body of POST /v1/enterprise/recording-policies. A recording policy is SEPARATE from the right to call, enterprise membership, Privacy Relay authorization and any meeting recording policy.

name.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

noticeRequired.description: Every participant must be notified (the server issues the notice: a realtime notice to application endpoints, a tone at the edge for SIP legs) before capture starts.

jurisdictionRef.description: Opaque reference to the compliance configuration this policy implements (e.g. NG-NDPA-2023/v2). Authoritative input from compliance / legal — the platform never infers recording law from a country. Never a telephone number.

maxRecordingSeconds.description: Maximum recording length in seconds (the recording then stops: MAX_DURATION).

isDefault.description: The scope's effective policy (one ACTIVE default).

calling.enterprise.v1.CreateRingGroupReq.description: Body of POST /v1/enterprise/ring-groups. fallback (EXTENSION, QUEUE or VOICEMAIL of the same scope) takes the SAME Call when no member answers.

name.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

calling.enterprise.v1.CreateVoicemailMai.description: Body of POST /v1/enterprise/voicemail/mailboxes. Requires an enterprise policy permitting voicemail.

calling.enterprise.v1.DayWindow.description: An open window inside one exception date (start before end).

end.description: Local wall-clock time HH:MM (24:00 = end of day).

calling.enterprise.v1.Department.description: An administrative / routing group of principals.

name.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

calling.enterprise.v1.DepartmentMemberIn.description: One member: an ACTIVE principal of the same scope (a foreign or unknown principal is 404).

calling.enterprise.v1.DepartmentRole.description: A member's organizational role (grants no scope or capability).

calling.enterprise.v1.Destination.description: A typed destination: an ACTIVE resource of the SAME tenant / application / environment (a foreign or unknown one is 404).

calling.enterprise.v1.DestinationType.description: Kinds of enterprise destination. SCHEDULE is a business-hours schedule (its OPEN / CLOSED route). PUBLIC_CONTACT is a registered public contact (an opaque Privacy Relay ContactReference; forwarding and closed-hours routes only), never a telephone number.

calling.enterprise.v1.EffectivePolicy.description: The policy in force for the environment: its ACTIVE default, else the restrictive built-in default (policyId null, version 0).

calling.enterprise.v1.EnterpriseCallCont.description: The safe enterprise context of a Call (create result and call history): the dialled extension's number and label as they were when the Call was placed (a snapshot that survives renumbering and offboarding), the policy version relied on, the routing phase, the current destination kind and the enterprise outcome. No member, device, provider or contact data.

extensionLabel.description: Bounded display name (no control characters, never a telephone number).

calling.enterprise.v1.EnterpriseIvrState.description: The IVR state of a Call (caller view): what the caller hears (recent built-in prompts) and may press (allowed keys) while a menu waits. Calling verifies the grant with Numbering (current state) and routes ONLY to the verified target. References and the bearer grant only — never the DCN, the caller's number or provider data.

scope.description: The assignment scope Numbering resolved the DCN to (verified by Calling with Numbering).

dcnResolution.description: Numbering's resolution as relayed (claims; Calling verifies them).

target.description: An opaque CF Meet routing target.

callerContactReference.description: The protected caller (opaque ContactReference issued by Privacy Relay's Contact Vault).

interconnectClass.description: The class of the route the call arrived on (default PUBLIC).

scope.description: The owner scope of the called relay number's session, from Privacy Relay's RESOLVED mapping.

callerContactReference.description: The protected caller (opaque ContactReference issued by Privacy Relay's Contact Vault).

allowedTargets.description: Whom Privacy Relay currently lets this caller reach (subject references). Calling re-checks current authority before creating the Call.
